notifications.body:
Both done: the undelivered-wake audit (answer to the question sent to wake-lead6) and the brief inspection of 972c6232.

AUDIT - IT IS TERMINAL TWICE, NOT ONCE, and the fix must touch two places. Full text: swarm context key 'audit/572-undelivered-root-wake-terminal' (seq 161995).

F1, the stronger half, which the framing misses: the durable KEY makes the outcome immutable. recordDelivery writes under key wake-root-delivery:${JSON.stringify([swarmId, wakeClass, seq])} and _append (coordination-ledger.mjs:1194-1195) does `const prior = store._byKey.get(key); if (prior) return prior;`. So the first outcome for an identity is the ONLY row that identity can ever have - a retry cannot append a delivered row, the store hands back the prior undelivered event. Fixing only alreadyRecorded would change nothing observable. (The docstring on deliverRootWakeOnce already claims 'at most once IN THIS RUNTIME'; the durable key actually spans incarnations.)
F2: the predicate suppresses before any write - alreadyRecorded matches kind wake.root_delivered OR wake.root_undelivered on (seq, wakeClass, swarmId).
F3, the harm that makes this urgent: BOTH identities are destination-blind. A wake that failed once is never delivered - not later by the same runtime, and not by the SUCCESSOR incarnation that comes up with a working session. On a deployment that reincarnates as often as this one, that is the likely case, not an edge.
F4: it contradicts the owed mechanism - root_owed says 'the root still owes this', and a terminal undelivered marker turns it into 'owed forever, delivered never, retried never', the shape the AGENTS law forbids.

FIX LADDER: (1) put the DESTINATION (harness + sessionId) in the delivery identity so a new session is a new identity; (2) make undelivered retryable under a bounded attempt generation, with attempt count and last failure on the row; (3) on cap exhaustion the state must become ATTENTION naming the wake and the failure, never silence; (4) if the operator wants strict at-most-once forever instead, the und

(Tail of the audit note, cut by the cap - the ladder and the serve verdict.)

FIX LADDER for the terminal undelivered wake: (1) put the DESTINATION (harness + sessionId) into the delivery identity so a new session is a new identity - that alone makes a successor incarnation eligible; (2) make undelivered RETRYABLE under a bounded attempt generation, recording the attempt count and the last failure on the row; (3) when the cap is exhausted the state must become ATTENTION naming the wake and the failure, never silence; (4) if the operator wants strict at-most-once forever instead, the undelivered path must page the operator rather than let a report look delivered.

What is right and should not change: exactly-once for a DELIVERED wake, keyed on the durable source row. The defect is only that a FAILURE was given the same terminal standing as a success.

ASSERTIONS to pin it: a transient failure followed by a working transport DELIVERS, and the record shows the attempt sequence; a same-destination retry either retries under a bounded generation or reports attention at the cap, never a silent no-op; delivered stays terminal; incarnation N's undelivered row does not block N+1; and a test on the key SHAPE itself so a future change cannot quietly reintroduce a destination-blind identity.

972c6232 - INSPECTED, CLEAN, no concerns: rootWakeTargetFromEnvironment parses BATON_ROOT_WAKE, returns null for absent or empty, refuses malformed JSON typed, and delegates to the shared validator; serveCheckout now builds advanced with integration.publishRemote preserved INDEPENDENTLY and rootWake only when non-null, passing advanced only when non-empty. Its pin reproduces: issue572-root-serve.test.mjs = 2 tests, 2 pass.

32b4806a closes both terminal layers: alreadyRecorded suppresses delivered only, recordDelivery keys include outcome kind (legacy failed key cannot occupy success), attachment retries pending reports automatically until success or caller shutdown, stable transport msg_id across attempts. Real store test572-w6 transientfail->automaticdelivery no new source passes; combined19/19. Please independently review it. I did NOT adopt attempt exhaustion/caps: #572 forbids moving live work to another unwoken party based on counters. New-target retry after failure works because failures no longer suppress any target; successfully delivered source rows retain existing terminal contract.

Retry fix committed32b4806a, independently audited precursor by rigidity-reviewer7: fixed both alreadyRecorded failure suppression AND immutable shared outcome key. Successful and failed receipt keys differ; failures retry via attachment until success/shutdown; msg_id stable across retries. Full delivery/wiring/serve19/19, new real-store automaticretry pin572-w6. No attempt cap (would recreate #572). Root serve configuration972c6232 still required for deployment.

Saw your callback implementation and collateral migrations in progress. Please include removal/update of expected-red manifest entries for every deleted or renamed policy pin (or report exact old/new names for me to do at union). Full union has inherited limits registry, so your frame-economics one-line policy delta will be preserved when merged. Ensure decision stop only stops the requested member/explicit scope; callback throw or invalid result must not mark done or stop live work.

#568 platform guards committed as 09c3e202. Linux scopes /proc cwd reads to process.getuid(), skips foreign uid and ENOENT/ESRCH races, and retains unreadable same-uid PIDs. macOS uses uid-filtered spawnSync lsof and rejects stderr/error/signal/invalid status. Git status/HEAD observation failures retain the row and continue. Final #568 14/14; worktree 36/36; no fixture remains. Running current-target+#561 composition before superseding publish.

Concrete review: current onCheckpoint stop for one role sets orchestratorStopped and breaks whole wave, whose finally closes every live peer. Callback is passed one member, so stop must stop that member/run and continue observing its peers. If intended wave-stop is needed, use separately explicit caller AbortSignal; do not widen per-member decision silently. Please add a two-member pin proving stop for member A does not stop B.

568 platform correction09c3e202 is ready; worker reports14/14 issue568 +36/36 worktree. Please verify required changes and settle forthcoming superseding contribution. I am merging it into union now; reviewer-requested Linuxuid/macstderr/status+HEAD retention all visibly changed. Root retry correction32b4806a was sent earlier; both failure predicate and immutable outcome key are fixed, with automatic retry and stable msg_id.

Corrected #568 contribution recorded: contribution-d8f3cd96c2f131184147cc4407b117b6 seq 163072, tip 09c3e202. Supersedes contribution-483a5b31. Final #568 14/14, worktree 36/36; master 3d851f9f + accepted #561 + #568 composes cleanly with platform guards 4/4.

One more contract check: explicit steering:none with no onCheckpoint still has no active decision consumer for a pausable member when embedded caller has no configured root. Do not preserve that as a silent waiting mode. Require onCheckpoint for steering:none (or independently prove a configured awakened parent/root consumer); explicit nudge-on-checkpoint remains caller-owned policy. Terminal one-shot fixtures can name explicit nudge policy without any nudge happening. Please cover no-consumer refusal before start.
